newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Harsh winter boosted Dutch 1996 natural gas sales.
newsitem.headline: Harsh winter boosted Dutch 1996 natural gas sales.

text.p: The harsh winter of 1995/1996 boosted Dutch monopoly natural gas supplier Nederlandse Gasunie NV's sales in 1996 by over 12 percent from the previous year, the company said on Thursday.

Gasunie supplied 93.7 billion cubic metres of gas to domestic and foreign customers in 1996 compared with 83.1 billion in 1995, a rise of 12.8 percent. Turnover rose to 18.7 billion guilders from 17 billion in 1995, the company said.
"The unusually cold winter of 1995/1996 was responsible for the growth of over 10 billion cubic metres in Gasunie's sales volume," it said.
On January 26, 1996, Gasunie recorded its highest ever daily sales volume of 545 million cubic metres of gas as temperatures averaged below minus 13 degrees centigrade.
Gasunie is 50 percent owned by the Dutch state, with Royal Dutch/Shell Group and Exxon Corp each holding 25 percent.
